- Overestimate prices in bullish sentiment periods (high sentiment > 0.5) — model tends to be too optimistic.
- Underestimate prices in bearish sentiment periods (sentiment < 0.2) — model underreacts to negative signals.
- Overshoot after sharp price spikes — model overreacts to recent highs, leading to overprediction.
- Lag in mean reversion — model takes too long to adjust downward after peaks, especially when sentiment is neutral or negative.
- Horizon-specific bias: 30-day forecasts consistently underestimate upward momentum in early periods (e.g., first 5–7 days) when sentiment is rising.
- When sentiment is high and price is rising, model often fails to capture the full momentum — underestimates the peak.
- When sentiment is low and price is falling, model often fails to recognize the depth of the drop — underestimates the trough.
- Model tends to smooth out volatility — underestimates short-term spikes and overestimates long-term trends in flat sentiment periods.
